15 The density of air on the Earth decreases almost linearly with height from 1.22 kg m–3 at sea level
to 0.74 kg m–3 at an altitude of 5000 m.
Atmospheric pressure at the Earth’s surface on a particular day is 100 000 Pa. The value of g
between the Earth’s surface and an altitude of 5000 m can be considered to have a constant
value of 9.7 m s–2.
What will be the atmospheric pressure at an altitude of 5000 m?
A
36 000 Pa
B
48 000 Pa
C
52 000 Pa
D
59 000 Pa

hints: Notice the air density is not constant: it falls from $1.22\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ to $0.74\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ over the $5000\text{ m}$ height, but the fall is described as almost linear.
Recall that pressure change with height is $\Delta p = \rho g h$, so for varying density you need the average density of the $5000\text{ m}$ column multiplied by $g = 9.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Calculate the mean density, then the weight of that air column, then subtract that pressure drop from the $100000\text{ Pa}$ surface pressure.
walkthrough: Identify the column of air between sea level and $5000\text{ m}$. Its height is $h = 5000\text{ m}$ and $g = 9.7\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Because density decreases almost linearly, use the average density: $\rho_{avg} = (1.22 + 0.74)/2 = 0.98\text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
The pressure drop across the column is the weight per unit area: $\Delta p = \rho_{avg} g h$.
Substitute values with units: $\Delta p = 0.98 \times 9.7 \times 5000 \approx 47530\text{ Pa}$.
Pressure falls with height, so $p_{5000} = p_{surface} - \Delta p \approx 100000 - 47530 \approx 52500\text{ Pa}$.
Rounded to the options given, this is about $52000\text{ Pa}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too low because it subtracts too large a pressure drop, for example by using sea-level density $1.22\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ for the whole $5000\text{ m}$ column.

B.explanation: Too low because it uses a density larger than the linear average, close to using only the higher sea-level value.

C.explanation: Equals surface pressure minus $\rho_{avg}gh$ with $\rho_{avg}=0.98\text{ kg m}^{-3}$, giving about $100000-47500 \approx 52000\text{ Pa}$.

D.explanation: Too high because it subtracts too small a pressure drop, for example by using the $0.74\text{ kg m}^{-3}$ top density for the whole column.
